title: The Delhi Sultanate: Five Dynasties, 320 Years

questions.question: Mahmud of Ghazni's most famous raid, the sack of the Somnath temple, took place in:
questions.rationale: Mahmud raided India seventeen times between 1000 and 1027; the sack of Somnath in 1025 was the most notorious, though he took plunder, not territory.

questions.question: At the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), Muhammad Ghori defeated:
questions.rationale: After losing the First Battle of Tarain in 1191, Ghori's mounted archers destroyed Prithviraj Chauhan's forces in 1192, opening north India to Turkish rule.

questions.question: The Sultanate's real institutional founder, who regularised the iqta and minted the tanka, was:
questions.rationale: Iltutmish (1211-1236) regularised the iqta, completed the Qutub Minar, issued the silver tanka and copper jital, and organised the Chahalgani.

questions.question: Which Sultan styled himself Zil-i-Ilahi, 'the shadow of God on earth'?
questions.rationale: Balban (1266-1287) ruled by blood and iron, destroyed the Chahalgani nobility, ran the barid spy system, and built the Diwan-i-Arz.

questions.question: Alauddin Khalji's market system was enforced by which officials?
questions.rationale: Prices in Delhi's separate markets for grain, cloth, and horses were fixed by the Diwan-i-Riyasat and enforced by the shahna-i-mandi.

questions.question: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's token currency of 1329 failed primarily because:
options: Counterfeit copper coins flooded the market
questions.rationale: Bronze tokens were declared equal in value to silver tankas, but easy counterfeiting flooded Delhi with fakes and the scheme was withdrawn within about four years.

questions.question: Ibn Battuta, who left an eyewitness account of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's court, was a traveller from:
questions.rationale: The Moroccan Ibn Battuta served as qazi of Delhi from 1333 to 1342 and recorded the age in his Rihla.

questions.question: Firuz Shah Tughlaq is remembered for all EXCEPT:
options: Five canals from the Yamuna and Sutlej
questions.rationale: Agra was founded by Sikandar Lodi in 1504. Firuz Shah's works were the canals, hospitals, and translations of Sanskrit medical texts.

questions.question: The Chishti order's most famous Delhi saint, patron of Amir Khusrau, was:
questions.rationale: Nizamuddin Auliya (d. 1325) of Delhi was the greatest Chishti shaikh of the capital; Muinuddin Chishti was the order's founder at Ajmer.

questions.question: The Sultanate ended in 1526 when Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at:
questions.rationale: Babur destroyed the Lodi army at the First Battle of Panipat on 21 April 1526, ending the Delhi Sultanate and founding Mughal rule.
